summary: Charleston County lookout: a 1939-40 tower, a 1956-57 steel replacement, and a 2011 auction sale with removal required.

facts.design: Steel structure, installed 1956-57 to replace an older wooden tower
facts.status_note: Sold at auction in February 2011 with removal required within 45 days. No source says whether it was removed.

events.note: State report for 1939-40: a new tower was constructed at the Johns Island site, with the Civilian Conservation Corps doing the tower construction.
State report for 1956-57: the old wooden tower was replaced by a new steel structure.
Sold at auction in February 2011 for $2,415.00 including taxes and fees; removal required within 45 days.

evidence.supports: Tower is a South Carolina Forestry Commission tower in Charleston County
Civilian Conservation Corps did the fire tower construction at no cost to the state
evidence.quote: All fire towers, tower buildings and telephone line construction was done by the Civilian Conservation Corps at no cost to the State or protective associations.

evidence.supports: 1939-40: a new tower was constructed at the Johns Island site
evidence.quote: A new tower was constructed at the Johns Island tower site in Charleston County.

evidence.supports: 1956-57: the old wooden tower was replaced by a new steel structure
evidence.quote: The old wooden tower located at Johns Island was replaced by a new steel structure.

evidence.supports: February 2011 auction sale for $2,415.00 including taxes and fees
evidence.quote: February 2011: The tower was sold at auction for a total of $2,415.00 including taxes and fees.

evidence.supports: Blog: the Johns Island Tower was among towers the agency was selling to the highest bidder
Blog: the agency was selling its lookout towers to the highest bidder
evidence.quote: It seems that the South Carolina Forestry Commission is selling several of its lookout towers to the highest bidder.
Bidding for the towers starts at $500.

evidence.supports: The purchaser was responsible for removing the tower
evidence.quote: The purchaser is responsible for removing the tower.

evidence.supports: The agency closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: Build and replacement dates come from a Forest Lookouts page quoting state Forestry Commission reports. The 1939-40 entry records a new tower but does not say whether the wooden tower replaced in 1956-57 is that one. The blog post is undated, so it cannot be placed in time relative to the February 2011 sale. No source says whether the tower was removed or what remains at the site. No height appears in any source. Brief coordinates (32.7306, -80.1044) were not checked against a second source.
